To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) two distinct types of rat MR mRNAs are transcribed from a single gene; (ii) the 5′ end of the rat MR mRNA differs in both types of transcripts; and (iii) a functional promoter directing expression of the novel type of rMRRNA in the brain has been isolated and characterized.

(i) we have identified a new type of rMR mRNA in rat hippocampus which differs from the classical type of MR mRNA by a different 5′untranslated region; (ii) we have isolated a genomic clone containing the protein coding exon of the rat MR as well as the 5′-flanking region of the gene; (iii) we have shown that this 5′-untranslated exon is expressed in hippocampus, whereas the classical type of rMR is expressed

the rat MR gene encodes a novel mRNA variant in the hippocampus which differs from the previously known MR mRNAs and that the 5′ flanking region of the MR gene contains cis‐elements that direct the tissue‐specific expression of the MR gene.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the elucidation of the molecular mechanisms that regulate the transcriptional activity of the mineralocorticoid (MR) and the glucocorticoid receptor gene in brain.
the identification of the molecular mechanisms involved in the regulation of the rat glucocorticoid receptor.
the identification and characterization of novel rat MR cDNAs and the promoter region of the rat MR‐gene.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the rat MR gene has a novel 5′‐promoter sequence that is active in the brain.
this is the first report of the cloning of a rat MR cDNA and of the identification of a novel rMR cRNA in the hippocampus.
the MR gene has a complex structure and that the MR gene is regulated in a complex manner.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
there is a functional promoter directing expression of a novel type of rat MR mRNA in brain.
the MR promoter region is a functional promoter, which directs expression of the MR gene in brain.

we have identified a novel type of rat mineralocorticid receptor (MR) cDNA that encodes a protein identical to that of a previously described MR cDNA but differs in its 5′ untranslated sequences.
we have identified a novel type of rat mineralocorticoids receptor (rMR).
